**brief station of few days**  
tick-tick, tick-tick; tick-tick, tick-tick...  
it is my train's wheels that so  rhythmically click
tick-tick, tick-tick; tick-tick, tick-tick...  
the compartment once full now is bare  
my fellow passengers have moved on, each in their own way  
some offered farewells, while others slipped away in silence;  
now I stretch out across the seat, my head pressed to the glass.  

tick-tick, tick-tick; tick-tick, tick-tick...  
I might as well doze off, as the rhythm lulls my head to nod  
tick-tick, tick-tick; tick-tick, tick-tick...  
my luggage stands ready, my ticket has been clipped  
the Conductor mapped my journey well ahead of time  
He’ll see to it I wake on cue  
to gather my last bits and bobs anew.  

tick-tick, tick-tick; tick-tick, tick-tick...  
my body aches and my spirit feels unwell  
tick-tick, tick-tick; tick-tick, tick-tick...  
this journey was long, and I feel drained and spent  
I think I'm ready to step down, but must first wait—who's in control?  
somewhere in the night my truck sways to the side of the road.
